findings.summary: Barium titanate (BaTiO3) is a ferroelectric ceramic whose crystal structure undergoes temperature-driven phase transitions between cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and rhombohedral forms. Its remarkable dielectric response stems from off-center displacements of Ti4+ ions within TiO6 octahedra, which cooperate to produce spontaneous polarization. These properties enable use in high-K capacitors, transducers, and nonlinear optics, though the material's behavior is strongly affected by particle morphology, dopants, and grain structure.

mechanisms.title: Ferroelectric off-center displacement
mechanisms.explanation: The Ti4+ ion moves off-center within the TiO6 octahedron, creating a permanent electric dipole. Cooperative alignment of these dipoles across the lattice yields spontaneous polarization and high dielectric permittivity.

mechanisms.title: Phase-transition-driven polarization
mechanisms.explanation: Temperature-dependent symmetry changes (cubic to tetragonal to orthorhombic to rhombohedral) control the direction and magnitude of Ti4+ displacements. Only non-cubic phases exhibit ferroelectricity, and the transitions alter crystal shape and volume.

unknowns: Exact atomic-scale mechanism driving cooperative Ti4+ distortions across grain boundaries
How abnormal grain growth specifically enhances permittivity beyond simple density effects
Long-term stability of ferroelectric domains under electrical biasing and thermal cycling
Precise role of dopants such as Sr in modifying the phase transition temperatures
